page: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a legacy storage-optimized virtual instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 Broadwell processor providing 8 virtual CPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. A primary architectural component is the inclusion of a 2,000 GB local magnetic hard disk drive (HDD), paired with a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest processing capabilities representative of its older Broadwell-era architecture. The instance delivered a single-core Stress-NG score of 883.18 and a multi-core score of 4,177.44, both placing in lower performance tiers relative to contemporary hardware. Similarly, Geekbench results recorded 904.0 points in single-core and 3,371.0 points in multi-core routines. Memory testing recorded uncached large-block read throughput of 38.02 GB/sec and write throughput of 22.65 GB/sec, while PassMark memory testing achieved a competitive 1,968.21 points. In specialized execution metrics, PassMark database operations reached 2,390.78, and Redis processing achieved 2.51 million SET operations per second.

Architectural tradeoffs center around dense local magnetic capacity over execution throughput and input/output latency. Because this instance features rotational HDD storage rather than high-IOPS NVMe solid-state drives, sequential data throughput is prioritized over rapid random access. The CPU profile lacks contemporary vector enhancements such as AVX-512 and AMX, bounding its computational and machine learning execution efficiency. For example, text generation on a medium 7B parameter LLM reaches only 5.14 tokens per second.

Qualitatively, the h1.2xlarge delivers capacity-oriented cost efficiency for systems requiring significant local disk space without the operational expense of solid-state storage. Given these hardware specifications and performance metrics, the instance is suitable for high-capacity sequential data processing, distributed log processing, MapReduce batch jobs, data warehousing staging nodes, and legacy storage-intensive applications.
description: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for capacity-intensive sequential workloads. Operating on the Xen hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 2.3 GHz, alongside 32 GB of system memory and a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. The platform integrates a 2,000 GB local HDD, providing substantial storage density without solid-state media overhead. Benchmark results reflect legacy Broadwell-era compute throughput, showing a PassMark CPU score of 6,218.11 and modest memory bandwidth of 38.02 GB/sec for uncached reads. Lacking AVX-512 instructions and discrete accelerators, its computing density is limited relative to modern alternatives. The instance is suited for batch processing, large-volume sequential file handling, distributed file systems, data lake ingestion, and log analysis tasks.
